title: Coordinate Bounding Box Generator
description: Generate a normalised bounding box from corner coordinates with the Coordinate Bounding Box Generator — min/max extent for queries and GIS. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, corners pasted in the wrong order — northeast first, southwest second — come out normalised to the same min/max box, because extents should not care about your paste order.
quick_answer: The Coordinate Bounding Box Generator builds a normalised bounding box from corner coordinates — the minimum and maximum latitude and longitude, in the order your query or GIS expects. Enter the corners and read the extent: four clean numbers, order-fixed, ready for APIs, tile requests and dataset clips.

body.t: Reports and READMEs state areas loosely ('from X to Y'). The generator turns prose corners into a queryable box — compare the
Servers want (min, min, max, max). Generate it once, correctly, instead of hand-sorting four numbers under time pressure.
Define the study area by its corners and clip — the generator's output is the clip's exact argument.
A box whose min exceeds its max is a bug wearing a costume. Regenerate and compare; the difference is the diagnosis.
Paste the northeast corner then the southwest, or the reverse — the normalised output is identical. Extents are sets, not sequences, and the generator treats them so.
Latitude pasted as longitude produces a box in the wrong ocean (or an invalid one). The generator's range checks catch the impossible cases before your API returns silence.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
The normalised minimum/maximum extent from given corner coordinates — sorted, validated and formatted for direct use.
Do I need an account?
No — corners in, extent out.
Can I use the result for professional work?
Yes — extent normalisation is mechanical and exact. Professional care goes into choosing the corners, which remains your geography.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 lat/lon throughout.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
Extents inherit the corners' accuracy. Extra decimals are formatting, not knowledge.
Corners crossing the date line?
A box spanning ±180° needs two extents in most systems; the generator's handling is stated in its output rather than silently wrapping.
One point only?
A single point makes a degenerate box (zero area) — for centre-plus-radius, the Bounding Box Calculator is the right shape.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Yes — the extent pastes into clip and filter dialogs; mind the target's axis order, labelled in the table on this page.
Boxes from a set of points?
Compute min/max over the set — the Coordinate Span Calculator covers the spread of a point set directly.
Why not just eyeball min/max?
Because humans transpose digits and axes under load. The generator exists so the boring step is never the broken step.
Negative longitudes order?
West is more negative: min_lon is the westernmost (smallest) value. The normalisation handles hemispheres mechanically.
